text:
The decreasing order of electrical conductivity of the following aqueous solutions is :

0.1 M Formic acid (A),

0.1 M Acetic acid (B),

0.1 M Benzoic acid (C)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
0.1 M Formic acid(HCOOH) (A),

0.1 M Acetic acid$(CH_{3}$COOH) (B),

0.1 M Benzoic acid$(C_{6}H_{5}$COOH) (C)

Conductivity (K) depends on no of ions present in unit volume of solution. When no of ions increases conductivity also increases.

Also no of ions depends on degree of dissociation($α$).

We know, $α$ = $\sqrt{\frac{K_{a}}{C}}$

For all solutions C = 0.1 M

So, $α$ depends on only $K_{a}$ here.

$K_{a}$ of HCOOH $= 10^{-4}$

$K_{a}$ of $CH_{3}$COOH = 1.8 $\times$ $10^{-5}$

and $K_{a}$ of $C_{6}H_{5}$COOH = 6 $\times$ $10^{-5}$

$\therefore$ $α$(HCOOH) > $α(C_{6}H_{5}$COOH) > $α(CH_{3}$COOH)

Therefore conductivity order = A > C > B
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
25 g of an unknown hydrocarbon upon burning produces 88 g of $CO_{2}$ and 9 g of $H_{2}O$. This unknown
hydrocarbon contains :
options: 18 g of carbon and 7 g of hydrogen
20 g of carbon and 5 g of hydrogen
22 g of carbon and 3 g of hydrogen
24 g of carbon and 1 g of hydrogen
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{x}H_{y} +$ $\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )O_{2}$ $\to$ xCO$_{2} +$ $\frac{y}{2}H_{2}O$

No of moles of $CO_{2}$ produced = $\frac{88}{44}$ = 2 mol

No of moles of $H_{2}O$ produced = $\frac{9}{18}$ = 0.5 mol

According to stoichiometric mole mole analysis :

$\frac{molesofCO_{2}}{x}=\frac{molesofH_{2}O}{\frac{y}{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2}{x}=\frac{0.5}{\frac{y}{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{2}{1}$

So, $\frac{noofatomsof{}^{'}C^{'}inC_{x}H_{y}}{noofatomsof{}^{'}H^{'}inC_{x}H_{y}}=\frac{2}{1}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{Massof{}^{'}C^{'}inC_{x}H_{y}}{Massof{}^{'}H^{'}inC_{x}H_{y}}=\frac{2\times 12}{1\times 1}=\frac{24}{1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
The coordination numbers of Co and Al in [$Co(Cl)(en)_{2}$]Cl and $K_{3}$[$Al(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}$], respectively, are :
(en = ethane-1, 2-diamine)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here in [$Co(Cl)(en)_{2}$]Cl

'Cl' is monodentate so one coordinate linkage will be made with Co.

'en' is bidentate so two coordinate linkage will be made with Co. There are two 'en ' present so 4 coordinate linkage will be made with Co.

$\therefore$ Total 5 coordinate linkage will be made with Co by Cl and en.  So C.N. of Co is 5.

Here in $K_{3}$[$Al(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}$]

$C_{2}O_{4}^{-2}$ is bidentate so two coordinate linkage will be made with Al. There are three $C_{2}O_{4}^{-2}'$ present so 6 coordinate linkage will be made with Al.

$\therefore$ So C.N. of Al is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text:
Thermal decomposition of a Mn compound (X) at 513 K results in compound Y, MnO$_{2}$ and gaseous product.
MnO$_{2}$ reacts with NaCl and concentrated $H_{2}SO_{4}$ to give a pungent gas Z. X, Y and Z, respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Potassium permanganate decomposes at 513 K:

$2~\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}{}^{513\mathrm{K}}\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}+\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$

So X is $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$, Y is $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}$ and the gaseous product is $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$.

$\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ oxidises the chloride in the presence of concentrated $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ to chlorine, the pungent gas Z:

$\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{NaCl}+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\longrightarrow \mathrm{MnSO}{}_{4}+2\mathrm{NaHSO}{}_{4}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$

$\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{MnO}{}_{4}$ does not give $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$, $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ and a gas on heating; it disproportionates to $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$ only in neutral or acidic solution.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

We know, $\Delta G^{o}=-RT\ln K$

Case 1 : 

If $\Delta G^{o}   0$

Case 2 :

text:
$NO_{2}$ required for a reaction is produced by the decomposition of $N_{2}O_{5}$ in CCl$_{4}$ as per the equation,

$2N_{2}O_{5}(g)$ $\to$ $4NO_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g)$.

The initial concentration of $N_{2}O_{5}$ is 3.00 mol $L^{–1}$
 and it is 2.75 mol $L^{–1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta [NO_{2}]}{\Delta [t]}$ = $+\frac{1}{120}\times \frac{4}{2}$ $= 0.01667 = 1.667 × 10^{–2}$

text:
A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.6 g of urea (molar mass = 60 g mol$^{–1})$ and 1.8 g of glucose (molar
mass = 180 g mol$^{–1})$ in 100 mL of water at $27^{o}C$. The osmotic pressure of the solution is :

(R = 0.08206 L atm $K^{–1}$
 mol$^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, osmotic pressure ($π$) = (Resultant molarity)$\times$R$\times$T

Resultant molarity = $\frac{Totalmolesofallsolutes}{Totalvolume(inlit)}$

= $\frac{\frac{0.6}{60}+\frac{1.8}{180}}{0.1}$ = 0.2 mol/lit

$\therefore$ Osmotic pressure ($π$) = (0.2)$\times$0.08206$\times$300 = 4.92 atm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot

text: In which one of the following equilibria, $K_{p}$ $\neq$ $K_{C}$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$K_{p} = K_{C}(RT)^{$\Delta ng}

$K_{p} = K_{C}$ when $\Delta n_{g} = 0$

$K_{p}$ $\neq$ $K_{C}$ when $\Delta n_{g}$ $\neq$ 0 and T $\neq$ 12 K

In this reaction, $2C(s) + O_{2}(g)$ ⇋ 2CO(g)

$\Delta n_{g} = 1$, so $K_{p}$ $\neq$ $K_{C}$
